title: PCIe-link-state-and-CPU-gov-interaction-bench-notes
content:
Summary:

This doc collects notes and early findings from a focused bench we ran to investigate intermittent p99 latency spikes that correlate with (a) host PCIe link state changes and (b) CPU frequency governor activity. The anomaly shows up across cloud SKUs (A100/H100/L40S families) but with different fingerprints.

Why we did this:
- Customer reports + internal alerts showed recurring small bursts of ~20–80ms extra p99 latency during long-context inference (prefill -> decode) on hosted clusters.
- Stacktrace/attribution often points to host-device transfers (kv cache writes) and kernel launch stalls.
- Hypothesis: a non-obvious interaction between PCIe link power-management (L0s/L1 entry/exit) and CPU freq scaling causes transient stalls when tiny host copy bursts arrive while the CPU is in a low-power state.

High-level hypothesis and goals:
- Hypothesis 1: Modern drivers and OS power heuristics favor aggressive PCIe link power-down on idle; when a burst occurs the link resume increases latency (and sometimes interacts with driver workqueues).
- Hypothesis 2: CPU frequency governor transitions (ondemand/ondemand-like or schedutil) can coincide with those DMA interrupts / user-space wakeups and amplify wallclock latency due to core wake latency and scheduling delays.
- Goal: reproduce reliably across skus, quantify contribution to p50/p95/p99, and suggest mitigations (pin CPU cores, change governor, disable L0s/L1 via sysfs, driver flags).

Test matrix and environment:
- SKUs tested: aws-p4d.24xlarge (A100), aws-p5.48xlarge (H100), gcp-a2-highgpu-1g (A100), gcp-h100-vm-standard-8 (H100), azure-L40s-standard-4 (L40S).
- CUDA drivers tested: 11.8, 12.1, 12.2; NVIDIA driver packages: 525.xx, 535.xx, 545.xx where available in-cloud images.
- OS kernels: 5.15 (default cloud images), 6.1 (custom), 6.4 (experimental) — we tried to measure kernel-level resume latencies.
- CPU governors: performance, powersave, ondemand (or equivalent), schedutil.
- Serving runtime: local daemon (serving-runtime v1.43.0 with continuous-batching enabled), model: 13B decoder-only, context sizes: 1k, 8k, 32k. Batch profiles: single-token decode at 8 concurrent requests, and large prefill bursts (batch size up to 4, seq len 32k prefills).
- Measurement: 10k requests per config, p50/p95/p99 capture, walltime traces (perf, eBPF uprobes for libc memcpy, NVML counters), PCIe link state logs (lspci -vvv), dmesg kernel timestamped logs.

Commands and knobs used (notes):
- To disable PCIe ASPM/L1: echo "off" > /sys/module/pcie_aspm/parameters/policy (varies by distro)
- To force CPU governor: cpupower frequency-set -g performance
- To pin process to core 0: taskset -c 0 ./serve_binary ...
- NVML capture: nvidia-smi dmon -s u -f /tmp/nvml.csv &
- eBPF tracer: perf record -a -e sched:sched_switch -e block:block_rq_issue -e cpu-frequency:cpu_frequency -o /tmp/perf.data &

Key findings (quantified):
- A100 (p4d / gcp-a2): With default images (ondemand/schedutil), we saw sporadic p99 spikes adding ~35–70ms during decode bursts. Disabling ASPM reduced p99 by ~22–35% in these scenarios. Switching CPU governor to performance removed ~15–25% of remaining spikes.
- H100 (p5 / gcp-h100): Baseline p99 already lower for small-batch decodes, but larger prefill bursts (32k) caused larger variance. H100 VBIOS/PCIe link handling appears to be more tolerant (fewer ASPM exits), but kernel IRQ storms on some images caused scheduling delays; CPU governor change to performance improved p99 by ~18% on average.
- L40S (azure): Showed highest sensitivity to link state changes; disabling ASPM yielded the largest win (~40% p99 reduction). We suspect the L40S firmware plus Azure host configs are more aggressive with link power savings.

Tracer evidence (high level):
- Timestamp aligned logs show an incoming host memcpy completed (kernel DMA completion) but user-space thread not scheduled until ~20–50ms later in several p99 cases. perf/trace shows cpu_frequency change events around these windows.
- eBPF/block events show the CPU entering deeper sleep states between prefill and decode phases for low-traffic runs; a prefill burst wakes the CPU and also triggers PCIe link resume. Both together line up with the p99 outliers.

Practical mitigations tested and tradeoffs:
1) System knobs: set cpu governor to performance and disable ASPM/L1. Outcome: most stable p99 but increased baseline power. Recommended for Dedicated or heavy-throughput Dedicated clusters.
2) Runtime-level: warmup micro-bursts before decode (1–2 tiny prefetch RPCs) to keep host link and CPU warm. Outcome: reduced spikes without OS changes; increases steady-state RPC count and slight cost.
3) Pinning batch IO threads to specific cores and raising their priority. Outcome: reduced scheduling jitter for critical copies, but complicates multi-tenant consolidation.
4) Driver-level: experiment with NV driver flags to prefer polling on small-copy completions (reduced wake scheduling). Some driver versions expose flags; result varied by driver.

Open questions / anomalies:
- On some AWS hosts, disabling ASPM had little effect (possible override by hypervisor). Need to confirm host firmware policies with cloud infra contacts.
- We saw one image/driver combo where p99 increased after switching to performance governor — likely due to CPU thermal throttling under long prefill; need thermal counters.
- L40S results might be confounded by different NIC offload config (RDMA vs TCP); need to re-run with identical networking stack where possible.

Next steps and experiments planned:
- Reproduce with synthetic microbench that isolates host->device memcpy latencies with minimal user-space scheduling involvement (kernel bypass tests).
- Test hybrid mitigation: small warmup RPC + soft affinity for IO threads and keep OS at ondemand but tweak tunables (e.g., /proc/sys/kernel/sched_migration_cost_ns).
- Open ticket with cloud partners: request host firmware/BIOS ASPM policy docs for p5/p4/L40S machines.
- Add continuous detector in Console: if we detect correlated pci_resume + cpu_freq_change + elevated decode p99, emit a specialized alert and suggested mitigations.

Quick reproducibility recipe (minimal):
1) Launch a p4d.24xlarge test instance with image X (link in linked_artifacts).
2) Install CUDA 12.1 + driver 535.xx.
3) Start runtime with model-13B, ctx 32k, prefill script that sleeps 2s between prefill and decode to let CPU idle.
4) Run 5k requests and grep perf log for cpu_frequency events around p99 timestamps.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Share kernel/perf traces with infra (Samir) and reach out to cloud partners for ASPM policy confirmation.
- Bake a small CI job in perf-bench that runs these knobs nightly on a single SKU and captures trends.
- Draft a short internal runbook for Dedicated cluster setup: recommended kernel, driver, and governor for low-p99 long-context workloads.

Appendix: Observed numeric snapshot (example)
- p4d, default: p50=12ms p95=26ms p99=86ms
- p4d, ASPM=off + perf-gov: p50=11ms p95=22ms p99=46ms
- p5, default: p50=9ms p95=18ms p99=55ms
- L40s, default: p50=14ms p95=31ms p99=110ms

If you want the raw perf.data and nvml CSVs for the runs above, see linked_artifacts PR where I uploaded a tarball (github PR attached).
